title: How one spec becomes a verified explainer
summary: Follow a JSON story through validation, deterministic rendering, and local artifact checks.

truthLadder.analogy: Think of the spec as a stage script: validation checks the cast list, and rendering performs the same script the same way every time.
truthLadder.technical: The validator resolves IDs and evidence references before render.mjs hashes the canonical JSON, escapes text, injects semantic content into a fixed template, and validates the resulting HTML.
truthLadder.caveat: This pipeline verifies structure, offline boundaries, and deterministic output; it does not prove that every source claim is factually correct.

teachBack.question: Why does validation run before and after rendering?
teachBack.answer: The first pass checks the story contract; the second checks that the produced HTML still obeys its offline and safety invariants.

teachBack.question: Does a passing local artifact count as published?
teachBack.answer: No. It is only generated and locally verified until a separate destination workflow publishes and reads it back.
